meta.title: Load test until it breaks: the three walls of a Kafka cluster
meta.story: A team ramps a healthy 3-broker Kafka cluster from 20 to 270 MB/s with the abort guard switched off, to learn exactly how it fails. Compressed: 1 s of playback ≈ 10 s of test time.

background.title: The system
background.body: A 3-broker Kafka cluster (b1, b2, b3), each with a 250 MB/s gp3 volume. The events topic has 48 partitions, replication factor 3, min.insync.replicas=2. Six load generators write 1 KB records with acks=all; a consumer group reads them live.

background.title: How it normally works
background.body: A produce request goes to the partition leader, which appends it; followers fetch from the leader. With acks=all the producer is acked once every in-sync replica (ISR) has the data. A follower that is behind for replica.lag.time.max.ms (30 s) is dropped from the ISR. If the ISR shrinks below min.insync.replicas, writes are rejected.

background.title: Today
background.body: Marta's team raises the load in 7-minute steps: 20, 60, 100, 150, 190, 230, 270 MB/s. The abort guard is off on purpose. They want to know which signal moves first, where it starts to hurt, and what 'broken' actually looks like.

learn: which signal moves first as load grows, and which moves last
why a cluster at 92% disk can lose its replicas
what 'broken' looks like to a producer using acks=all
where a safe steady-state ceiling really sits

dashboard.title: Throughput
dashboard.why: Offered is what we push, acked is what the cluster accepted. The gap between them is the break.

dashboard.title: Produce p99 latency
dashboard.why: What a producer feels. It rises long before anything fails, so it is the early warning.

dashboard.title: Producer send errors
dashboard.why: Rejected or timed-out sends. Zero for most of the test, then the cliff.

dashboard.title: Request handler idle (b1)
dashboard.why: How much spare capacity b1's request threads have. Under 30% means requests queue.

dashboard.title: Broker CPU (b1)
dashboard.why: Shows b1 working harder than its share. Rules out 'the whole cluster is CPU bound'.

dashboard.title: Disk throughput per broker
dashboard.why: With RF 3 on 3 brokers this equals the produce rate. The volume cap is the physical ceiling.

dashboard.title: Follower fetch lag
dashboard.why: How far followers trail their leaders. Past 30 s a follower is dropped from the ISR.

dashboard.title: Replication health
dashboard.why: Under-replicated is a warning; below min.insync.replicas means producers are being rejected.

dashboard.title: Consumer lag
dashboard.why: Stayed small the whole test, so lag would never have warned us about the failure.

dashboard.title: Request queue time p99 (b1)
dashboard.why: Time requests wait for a free handler. The first place saturation shows up.

dashboard.title: Dirty page cache
dashboard.why: Data accepted but not yet on disk. At vm.dirty_ratio the kernel blocks writers.

dashboard.title: Disk await
dashboard.why: Per-I/O wait. Near saturation it grows far faster than throughput does.

dashboard.title: Producer buffer used
dashboard.why: buffer.memory is shared by all partitions, so a few sick partitions can starve the rest.

dashboard.title: Broker GC pause p99
dashboard.why: Rules out the usual suspect: pauses stay in tens of ms, so GC is not why followers stalled.

beat.hint: Three brokers, one topic of 48 partitions, each stored three times. Six load generators send 20 MB/s of 1 KB records with acks=all. Everything is boring: p99 about 9 ms, brokers mostly idle. The plan is to raise the load in steps until something gives.
beat.deep: events: 48 partitions, RF 3, min.insync.replicas=2. Producers: acks=all, linger.ms=5, batch.size=128 KB, buffer.memory=32 MB each. Brokers: num.replica.fetchers=1, replica.lag.time.max.ms=30000, auto.leader.rebalance.enable=false.

notes.text: Offered = acked = consumed: the cluster keeps up
Baseline p99 about 9 ms at 20 MB/s
Handlers 92% idle: plenty of headroom

feed.text: ramp plan: 20 > 60 > 100 > 150 > 190 > 230 > 270 MB/s, 7 min holds, 1 KB records, acks=all. abort guard is OFF on purpose. I want to see how it breaks, not where we stop.
$ kafka-topics.sh --describe --topic events | head -1  > PartitionCount: 48  ReplicationFactor: 3  Configs: min.insync.replicas=2,retention.ms=86400000,segment.bytes=1073741824
$ kafka-producer-perf-test.sh --topic events --record-size 1000 --throughput 20000 --producer-props acks=all linger.ms=5 batch.size=131072 buffer.memory=33554432  (x6 hosts)
ramp step 2/7: 60 MB/s (60k rec/s), hold 7 min
INFO [Log partition=events-12, dir=/data/kafka] Rolled new log segment at offset 4411203 in 3 ms
ramp step 3/7: 100 MB/s (100k rec/s), hold 7 min
JMX kafka.network:type=RequestMetrics,name=TotalTimeMs,request=Produce  99thPercentile=12.0  Mean=4.1
100 MB/s: p99 12 ms, busiest broker at 40% CPU. boring graphs, my favourite kind.
ramp step 4/7: 150 MB/s (150k rec/s), hold 7 min

beat.hint: From 20 to 150 MB/s the cluster scales linearly: acked tracks offered, p99 stays under 20 ms. With RF 3 on 3 brokers each disk writes one full copy of the stream, so disk MB/s equals produce MB/s. But b1's handlers went from 92% to 42% idle: a quiet early warning.
beat.deep: b1 leads 28 of 48 partitions (28/12/8). Leadership drifted during the last rolling restart and auto.leader.rebalance.enable=false keeps it that way, so b1 does 58% of the produce work and serves the follower fetches for those partitions.

notes.text: Acked tracks offered 1:1 up to 150 MB/s
Disk MB/s = produce MB/s (RF 3 on 3 brokers)
b1 handlers 92% to 42% idle: the quiet warning
p99 9 to 19 ms: still well inside budget

feed.text: $ kafka-topics.sh --describe --topic events | awk '{print $6}' | sort | uniq -c  >  28 Leader: 1   12 Leader: 2   8 Leader: 3
150 is clean: p99 19 ms. b1 handler idle is dropping though, 42%. going to 190.
ramp step 5/7: 190 MB/s (190k rec/s), hold 7 min
JMX RequestHandlerAvgIdlePercent=0.27  NetworkProcessorAvgIdlePercent=0.51  (num.io.threads=8, num.network.threads=3)

beat.hint: At 190 MB/s b1's request handlers are mostly busy. The disks are fine (76% of cap); the cluster is lopsided: b1 leads 58% of the partitions, so it takes most produce and replica-fetch traffic. Requests queue and p99 more than doubles. Nothing has failed yet.
beat.deep: Rule of thumb: alert when RequestHandlerAvgIdlePercent < 30%, saturated near 20%. Queue time p99 on b1 is 45 ms; produce p99 = queue + local append + wait for followers + response.

notes.text: b1 handlers under 30% idle: requests wait in a queue
p99 19 to 48 ms: queueing, not slow disks
b1 CPU 78%: it carries 58% of the leader work
Queue time 4 to 45 ms

feed.text: ramp step 6/7: 230 MB/s (230k rec/s), hold 7 min
$ iostat -x 1 nvme1n1  >  w/s 228k-iops-eq  wMB/s 228.4  w_await 18.2  %util 92.1
p99 is 400 ms and the disks are 92% busy. let's bump num.io.threads and num.network.threads and redo the step.

beat.hint: At 230 MB/s each disk is 92% busy against its 250 MB/s cap. Writes wait behind writeback, p99 jumps to about 400 ms and followers start to trail. More I/O or network threads is the tempting fix, but they would only wait on the same disk.
beat.deep: Dirty pages climb to 2.4 GB (background writeback starts at 3.2 GB, writers block at vm.dirty_ratio = 6.4 GB). Disk await 3 to 18 ms: near saturation, queueing delay grows steeply.

notes.text: 230 of 250 MB/s: 92% of the volume cap
p99 about 400 ms: writes queue behind the disk
Followers trail 9 s: stalls while the disk is busy
Dirty pages 1.1 to 2.4 GB: writeback is behind

feed.text: INFO [Log partition=events-7, dir=/data/kafka] Rolled new log segment at offset 88197320 in 1480 ms

timeline.title: Ramp: 270 MB/s, above the disk cap

feed.text: ramp step 7/7: 270 MB/s (270k rec/s). volume cap is 250 MB/s.
INFO [Partition events-7 broker=1] Shrinking ISR from 1,2,3 to 1,2. Leader: (highWatermark: 88213110, endOffset: 88213441). Out of sync replicas: (brokerId: 3, endOffset: 88197320).
INFO [Partition events-7 broker=1] Shrinking ISR from 1,2 to 1. Leader: (highWatermark: 88213110, endOffset: 88214002). Out of sync replicas: (brokerId: 2, endOffset: 88197902).
WARN [Producer clientId=perf-3] Got error produce response with correlation id 91274 on topic-partition events-7, retrying (2147483646 attempts left). Error: NOT_ENOUGH_REPLICAS
every error is NOT_ENOUGH_REPLICAS. can we set min.insync.replicas=1 so the test can finish? or add a 4th broker?
INFO: task ReplicaFetcherThread-0-1:1873 blocked for more than 120 seconds.  (kernel: balance_dirty_pages throttling)
ERROR [Producer clientId=perf-3] org.apache.kafka.common.errors.TimeoutException: Expiring 128 record(s) for events-7:120003 ms has passed since batch creation  (delivery.timeout.ms=120000)

beat.hint: At 270 MB/s the disks can't drain the load. Dirty pages hit the 6.4 GB limit and followers stall past 30 s. b3, then b2, leave the ISR of b1's 28 partitions: one replica, below min.insync.replicas=2, so every write is rejected. Retrying batches then fill the shared producer buffer and starve even the healthy partitions.
beat.deep: min.insync.replicas=1 would hide the errors by acking single-copy writes; a 4th broker means copying terabytes through these saturated disks. With unclean.leader.election.enable=false, losing b1 now takes 28 partitions offline.

notes.text: Below min ISR 0 to 28, under-replicated 0 to 44
118k rec/s rejected: NOT_ENOUGH_REPLICAS
Acked falls 245 to 38 MB/s while offered stays 270
Followers 40 to 60 s behind: past the 30 s limit
Buffers full of retrying batches

feed.text: test aborted by Marta: all 6 generators stopped
$ kafka-topics.sh --describe --under-min-isr-partitions  >  Topic: events Partition: 7 Leader: 1 Replicas: 1,2,3 Isr: 1   (28 lines)
INFO [Partition events-7 broker=1] Expanding ISR from 1 to 1,2
INFO [Partition events-7 broker=1] Expanding ISR from 1,2 to 1,2,3

timeline.title: Healing starts when the load stops

beat.hint: Marta stopped the test. Producers drained, but healing took about six more minutes: followers had to re-fetch the gap while the disks were still busy. Once each caught up to the high watermark it re-entered the ISR. Below-min-ISR cleared first, then under-replicated.
beat.deep: A follower re-enters the ISR once its log end offset reaches the leader's high watermark. num.replica.fetchers=1 and the busy disks set the catch-up speed; no config change was needed.

notes.text: Below min ISR 28 to 0 as b2 rejoins, then URP to 0
Follower lag drains from 62 s to 0 once load is off
Disk stayed busy until catch-up finished

feed.text: ISR is whole. rebalancing leaders now: kafka-leader-election --election-type PREFERRED --all-topic-partitions. b1 should stop leading 58% of everything.
$ kafka-leader-election.sh --bootstrap-server b1:9092 --election-type PREFERRED --all-topic-partitions  >  Successfully completed leader election (PREFERRED) for partitions events-0 ... events-47
re-test: 175 MB/s (70% of the 250 MB/s volume cap), 10 min hold
175 MB/s: p99 14 ms, b1 handlers 52% idle, CPU 44%. boring again.
JMX RequestHandlerAvgIdlePercent=0.52  UnderReplicatedPartitions=0  UnderMinIsrPartitionCount=0  Produce 99thPercentile=14.0
holding 175. three numbers for the write-up: where it hurts (150 to 190), where it breaks (270), where we run it (175).

beat.hint: With leaders rebalanced (16/16/16) and the load at 175 MB/s, 70% of the disk cap, p99 is 14 ms, handlers are about 50% idle, and 75 MB/s of disk is spare for catch-up after a restart. It hurt at 150 to 190, broke at 270, and is safe at 175: three different numbers.
beat.deep: Why 70%: after a broker restart its replicas re-fetch the gap while still taking new writes, and that extra traffic shares the same 250 MB/s. Re-run the same ramp to confirm before trusting the number.

notes.text: p99 back to about 14 ms at 175 MB/s
Handlers about 50% idle: balancing moved the wall
175 of 250 MB/s: 75 MB/s spare
b1 CPU 44%, was 78% at 190 MB/s

feed.text: writing it up. next: same ramp with a broker killed mid-step.

report.tldr: Ramping a 3-broker Kafka from 20 to 270 MB/s: it got slow at 150 to 190 MB/s (a hot leader), saturated its disks at 230, and broke at 270 when stalled followers left the ISR and producers starved. A safe steady-state is about 175 MB/s.

chain.text: Offered 270 MB/s > 250 MB/s disk cap per broker
Dirty pages hit vm.dirty_ratio: writers stall
Followers stall > 30 s and leave the ISR
Retries fill the shared buffer, starving all
Stop load, let followers catch up, rebalance leaders

loop.label: retries burn handlers, stalls last longer

learnings.title: Find the knee, not the cliff
learnings.body: p99 and handler idle moved 80 MB/s before anything failed. Plan capacity from the knee.

learnings.title: Balance leaders before you benchmark
learnings.body: A 28/12/8 leader skew made b1 the early bottleneck. Enable auto.leader.rebalance or run preferred election.

learnings.title: Alert on p99 and under-min-ISR
learnings.body: Consumer lag stayed under 50k msgs the whole time. It measures consumers, not producers.

learnings.title: Keep 30% of the disk spare
learnings.body: Restarts and catch-up share the same volume. A 70% ceiling leaves room to heal.

math.title: Where the numbers come from
lines: RF 3 on 3 brokers: each disk writes one full copy, disk MB/s = produce MB/s
28 of 48 partitions led by b1 = 58% of produce work (fair share 33%)
volume cap 250 MB/s; offered 270 MB/s: +20 MB/s piles up as dirty pages
(6.4 GB dirty_ratio - 2.4 GB) / 20 MB/s = 200 s to block writers

myths.truth: Lag stayed small while producers failed. Watch produce p99, under-replicated and under-min-ISR partitions.

myths.myth: Set min.insync.replicas=1 so the test passes.
myths.truth: Errors vanish because writes are acked with one copy. The first broker loss then loses data.

myths.myth: More io/network threads will fix it.
myths.truth: The threads were waiting on a saturated disk; more of them only adds queueing.

config: min.insync.replicas=2          # keep; 1 trades durability for a green test
replica.lag.time.max.ms=30000  # how long a stalled follower stays in the ISR
num.replica.fetchers=1         # raise if one fetcher thread limits catch-up
auto.leader.rebalance.enable=true   # was false: let leadership self-heal
vm.dirty_background_ratio=10 / vm.dirty_ratio=20   # writers block at 6.4 GB here
delivery.timeout.ms=120000 / max.block.ms=60000    # how long a stuck producer holds on
runbook: Check leader balance first: describe the topic and count Leader: per broker.
Compare RequestHandlerAvgIdlePercent and disk %util: handlers or disk?
Do not lower min.insync.replicas or add brokers mid-incident.
Stop or cut the load, wait for ISR to refill, then re-run at 70% of the knee.
